analysis.study: CC-5013-MCL-001-PK (sponsor population PK and exposure-response report dated 8 October 2012)
analysis.population_quote: A total of 147 subjects from 7 studies contributed 2495 samples to the PPK analysis.
analysis.method: logistic regression of grade 3 or 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia on ln AUC, with disease and baseline counts
analysis.key_variables_quote: Type of hematological malignancy, lenalidomide exposure (lnAUC), and baseline cell counts (neutrophils or platelets) were the key variables contributing to the probability of experiencing Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia.

grade_3_4_thrombocytopenia.quote: In patients with MM, lenalidomide lnAUC was a significant predictor of Grade 3 or 4 thrombocytopenia after accounting for the effect of baseline platelet count (Odds Ratio for one lnAUC increase = 2.972 [95% CI: 1.027, 8.598]).

grade_3_4_neutropenia.quote: In patients with MM, the probability of experiencing Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia tended to increase with increased lenalidomide exposure (lnAUC), though this relationship did not reach statistical significance (Odds Ratio for one lnAUC increase = 1.982 [95% CI: 0.924, 4.249]).

not_reported: exact AUC definition (time window, model used to derive it)
number of myeloma patients in the analysis
consequence: Absolute probabilities cannot be computed. Only relative odds between two exposures, for patients with the same disease and baseline count, follow from the odds ratio.

derivation.relative_odds: OR_rel = OR ** (ln AUC_patient - ln AUC_reference) = (AUC_patient / AUC_reference) ** ln(OR)
derivation.units: Independent of AUC units and of a constant AUC scale factor, because only the ratio enters.
derivation.confidence_interval: Same formula with each CI limit of the odds ratio (monotonic in the odds ratio for a fixed AUC ratio).

supersedes.change: Adds the Chen 2017 review, reconciles its pooled odds ratio with the TGA myeloma-only value, and records that the relationships were not apparent in cycle 1.

second_source.citation: Chen N, Zhou S, Palmisano M. Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Lenalidomide. Clin Pharmacokinet. 2017;56(2):139-152.

quotes.design: the relationship between lenalidomide AUC and grade 3/4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia was examined in a meta-analysis ... including patients with MM, MDS, or MCL from six clinical studies over the dose range 5-50 mg
quotes.adjustment: After adjusting for disease and baseline cell counts, and including all treatment cycles up to 1 year
quotes.thrombocytopenia: lenalidomide AUC was a significant predictor of grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (odds ratio [OR] 3.337, 95 % CI 1.183-9.415)
quotes.neutropenia: and was also associated with increased grade 3/4 neutropenia (OR 1.978, 95 % CI 0.999-3.917)
quotes.cycle_1: These relationships were not apparent during the first treatment cycle.

second_source.cited_primary: Chen N, Ette E, Zhou S, Weiss D, Palmisano M. Population pharmacokinetics and exposure-safety of lenalidomide in patients with MM, MDS, and MCL. Blood. 2013;122:3234 (meeting abstract).

reconciliation.conclusion: Same sponsor exposure-safety analysis (CC-5013-MCL-001-PK; Blood 2013 abstract 3234), reported two ways: TGA gives the myeloma-only odds ratios (thrombocytopenia 2.972), Chen 2017 the all-disease estimate adjusted for disease (3.337). They are consistent; the myeloma-only value is used for myeloma.
reconciliation.remaining_difference: TGA describes 7 studies and 147 subjects in the population PK analysis; Chen describes six studies in the exposure-safety meta-analysis. The exposure-safety set may be a subset; not resolved.

time_window.statement: The odds ratios describe grade 3/4 events over all treatment cycles up to 1 year; the relationships were not apparent in the first cycle (Chen 2017).
time_window.consequence: Relative odds apply to a course of treatment, not to cycle 1.
